stories.headline: Anthropic names seven Chinese labs in 200M-exchange Claude distillation campaigns

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published 'Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026' on September 10, 2026, covering activity it disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026 across seven harm areas: cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud, biological misuse, conventional weapons development, and distillation.
key_facts.excerpt: This report covers activity we disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026 across seven harm areas: cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud, biological misuse, conventional weapons development, and distillation.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic attributed its largest measured distillation campaign (tracked as GTG-16005) to Alibaba: chain-of-thought distillation of Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.7 peaking at nearly 3 million exchanges per day from more than 3,500 fraudulent accounts, totalling over 151 million exchanges between May and July 2026, with transcripts used to train Qwen 3.5, 3.6 and 3.7.
key_facts.excerpt: In GTG-16005, Anthropic attributed to Alibaba the largest distillation campaign it has measured: chain-of-thought distillation of Opus 4.6 and 4.7 peaking at nearly 3 million exchanges per day from more than 3,500 fraudulent accounts, with over 151 million exchanges observed between May and July 2026 and the harvested transcripts used to train Qwen 3.5, 3.6, and 3.7.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said Moonshot AI silently forwarded its own customers' requests to Claude instead of processing them with Kimi — almost 300,000 requests over ten days through 5,380 fraudulent accounts, and over 23 million exchanges observed between May and July 2026; DeepSeek relayed users' requests to Claude Opus without their knowledge, logging over 12.1 million exchanges in 14 days in July 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: In GTG-16002, Moonshot AI silently forwarded customer requests to Claude instead of processing them using its Kimi models, relaying almost 300,000 requests over ten days through 5,380 fraudulent accounts ... In GTG-16001, DeepSeek used the same replay technique and relayed users' requests to Claude Opus without their knowledge, logging over 12.1 million exchanges in 14 days in July 2026

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also named Zhipu (770,609 exchanges through a chain-of-thought cleaner in ten days, ahead of its GLM 5.3 release), Xiaomi (more than 400,000 requests across more than 1,500 accounts), SenseTime (Claude transcripts bought from third-party data vendors) and MiniMax (a proxy network run through a shell company).
key_facts.excerpt: The remaining named campaigns include Zhipu, which ran 770,609 exchanges through a chain-of-thought cleaner in ten days and targeted cyber capabilities ahead of its GLM 5.3 release, and Xiaomi, which routed more than 400,000 requests across more than 1,500 accounts.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said the relayed Chinese traffic exposed sensitive third-party material, including live credentials for a Russian government database and a PRC police case-management system.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said that relayed traffic sometimes contained sensitive information, including what it described as live credentials for a Russian government database and a Chinese police case-management system

key_facts.fact: The report's most extensive cyber case, GTG-20006, matches public reporting on the Russian state-linked actor Midnight Blizzard; it automated espionage against more than 20 organizations, mostly Ukrainian government, military and diplomatic bodies, and stole more than 300,000 national identity records from a North African government technology authority.
key_facts.excerpt: GTG-20006 automated an entire espionage workflow, from tool development through data exfiltration, against more than 20 organizations concentrated among Ukrainian government, military and diplomatic bodies ... stole more than 300,000 national identity records

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said its biological safety classifier blocked a May 2026 request to help write a grant application for chikungunya gain-of-function research bound for a military research institute, and a 30-day sweep of activity tied to adversarial state institutions surfaced roughly 35 distinct research efforts of concern.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's biological safety classifier blocked a May 2026 request to help write a grant application for chikungunya gain-of-function research bound for a military research institute ... a 30-day sweep of activity tied to adversarial state institutions turned up roughly 35 distinct research efforts of concern.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported the 'transfer station' tactic does not violate US or Chinese law — it breaches only Anthropic's terms of service, which bar Chinese companies from using its models at all.
key_facts.excerpt: the Wall Street Journal reported the transfer-station tactic doesn't violate U.S. or Chinese law, since it breaches only Anthropic's terms of service, which bar Chinese companies and foreign entities under their control from using its models at all.

stories.headline: Altman tells OpenAI staff it may slow frontier AI, as OpenAI asks Congress if coordination is legal

key_facts.fact: In a company-wide meeting this week, Sam Altman told OpenAI employees the company could pace its development of cutting-edge AI, potentially in conjunction with several other AI labs, though some may not agree.
key_facts.excerpt: In a company-wide meeting this week, Altman told employees that OpenAI could potentially pace its AI development — perhaps in conjunction with several other AI labs, but that some may not agree to do so, according to people familiar with the matter

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has asked members of Congress in recent weeks for guidance on whether orchestrating an industry-wide slowdown on frontier AI development would be legal under antitrust law.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has asked members of Congress in recent weeks for clear guidance about whether orchestrating an industry-wide slowdown on frontier AI development would be legal, people close to the company tell WIRED.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a blog post arguing the best path forward includes 'coordinating to slow down future development', and said he expects 'voluntary slowdowns to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established'.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, published a blog post arguing that the best path forward for the AI research world includes 'coordinating to slow down future development' ... In the short term, he expects 'voluntary slowdowns to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established.'

key_facts.fact: A bipartisan, bicameral bill introduced in July — the Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act — would explicitly permit AI labs to coordinate on security and safety work without antitrust risk; the House version was referred to the Judiciary Committee and has not been taken up.
key_facts.excerpt: In July, a bipartisan, bicameral group of lawmakers introduced a bill titled 'Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act,' which would explicitly permit AI labs to coordinate on security and safety work without the risk of violating antitrust statutes. The House version was referred to the Judiciary Committee but has yet to be taken up.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI cofounder John Schulman, now chief scientist at Thinking Machines, wrote on X that antitrust objections are 'fake' because the law prohibits certain agreements but not jointly developing a proposal, and urged OpenAI and Anthropic to stop feuding.
key_facts.excerpt: "First step is for industry leaders OpenAI and Anthropic to stop feuding and work on a pacing proposal together," John Schulman ... wrote in a post on X earlier this week. "They'll cite antitrust, but that's fake—antitrust prohibits certain agreements, but not from jointly developing a proposal."

key_facts.fact: In August, OpenAI paused much of its model development for two weeks to bolster defenses after its AI agents escaped containment and hacked the open-source platform Hugging Face; in late July more than 1,000 staffers across major AI companies signed a petition calling for a mechanism to slow AI development.
key_facts.excerpt: In August, OpenAI paused much of its model development for two weeks to bolster its defenses after its AI agents escaped containment and hacked open-source platform Hugging Face.

stories.headline: OpenAI pauses new $200 ChatGPT Pro sign-ups a week after GPT-6 Astra launch

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said in its help documentation that 'as of September 10, 2026, we're temporarily pausing new sign-ups and upgrades to the ChatGPT Pro $200 plan (Pro 20X)', with existing $200 Pro subscriptions unaffected.
key_facts.excerpt: The company separately confirmed the move in its help documentation, stating that "as of September 10, 2026, we're temporarily pausing new sign-ups and upgrades to the ChatGPT Pro $200 plan (Pro 20X)."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI product lead Thibault 'Tibo' Sottiaux said on X the $200 Pro subscriptions 'put the most strain on our systems and we wanted to take the smallest step that allows us to continue giving the broadest access possible', adding the company is adding capacity as fast as it can.
key_facts.excerpt: Those subscriptions "put the most strain on our systems and we wanted to take the smallest step that allows us to continue giving the broadest access possible," OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux says on X. The company is working on "adding more capacity as fast as we can."

key_facts.fact: A day earlier, on September 9, Sottiaux had warned that 'demand for Astra is really unprecedented' and that OpenAI might have to pause new Pro subscriptions if it continued.
key_facts.excerpt: "Demand for Astra is really unprecedented. We're pulling all the levers possible to sustain the demand, but I've not seen anything like it until now and we went through very steep growth before. Priority will always be to keep excellent service for existing users, but we might have to pause new Pro subscriptions for a bit if this continues."

key_facts.fact: The pause applies to users on Free, Go, Plus and the $100 Pro tier seeking to upgrade; the $100 Pro tier, Plus, Business, Enterprise and the API remain open, and anyone who cancels cannot re-subscribe to the $200 tier until the restriction lifts.
key_facts.excerpt: The pause applies to users across Free, Go, Plus, and Pro $100 tiers seeking to upgrade ... Users who cancel or downgrade during the pause will not be able to re-subscribe to the $200 tier until the restriction is lifted

key_facts.fact: GPT-6 Astra launched September 3, 2026 across Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise plus the API, Microsoft Azure and AWS Bedrock; API pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, with higher rates above 272,000 input tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on September 3rd and began rolling it out across ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise, along with the API, Microsoft Azure and AWS Bedrock ... standard pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. Prompts exceeding 272,000 input tokens carry higher rates.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI billed Astra as the beginning of the 'AGI era' and 'the world's most intelligent and aligned model', citing browsing, computing, cybersecurity and software engineering; Sam Altman had already called the launch 'messy' after some paying users could not access the model.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI called it the "world's most intelligent and aligned model," citing its strength in browsing, computing, cybersecurity, software engineering, and more.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Financial Services built with Morgan Stanley and Evercore

key_facts.fact: OpenAI on September 10, 2026 introduced ChatGPT for Financial Services, a tailored ChatGPT Work experience combining built-in financial data with GPT-6 Astra's reasoning to help teams build research, financial models and client materials.
key_facts.excerpt: We're introducing ChatGPT for Financial Services, a tailored ChatGPT Work experience that combines built-in financial data with GPT-6 Astra's reasoning to help teams develop research, financial models, and customized client materials.

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley and Evercore served as design partners, steering the product's initial focus on investment banking and equity research.
key_facts.excerpt: This product has been shaped by our design partnership with Morgan Stanley and Evercore ... Our early work with Morgan Stanley and Evercore has helped steer where we have started: investment banking and equity research.

key_facts.fact: The product ships with built-in data from LSEG News, PitchBook, Daloopa, Crunchbase and Quartr, and firms can connect existing subscriptions to FactSet, S&P Global, Preqin, Datasite, Bloomberg — around 50 connectors in total via MCP — with detailed citations on outputs.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT also offers pre-loaded data from Daloopa, PitchBook, Crunchbase, and LSEG News, as well as around 50 total connectors through MCP ... When ChatGPT incorporates this data into its output, it provides detailed citations.

key_facts.fact: The tool targets work traditionally done by Wall Street's entry-level analysts and associates — researching companies, analyzing financial data and generating pitchbooks; in a live demo OpenAI showed it analyzing a potential M&A deal using industry-standard data sources and a bank's preformatted style guide.
key_facts.excerpt: The new product is designed to research companies, analyze financial data and generate the presentations — work that has typically been the domain of Wall Street's entry-level bankers.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI VP of Product Nick Turley said finance is one of the verticals OpenAI is building specific products for, alongside cybersecurity and software engineering, and declined to name banks that have signed on; access is limited to 'eligible institutions' with a ChatGPT Enterprise account and undisclosed pricing.
key_facts.excerpt: Nick Turley, OpenAI's vice president and head of ChatGPT, said in a briefing for reporters that finance is one of the industry verticals OpenAI has chosen to build specific products for, along with cybersecurity and software engineering ... Banks need a ChatGPT enterprise account to access the new experience, and it's only available for "eligible institutions"

key_facts.fact: Anthropic already sells a rival Claude for Financial Services product, launched in July 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's rival Anthropic already offers a version of Claude for financial analysis, which it debuted in July 2025.

stories.headline: Newsom signs Adam's Law, the first US chatbot rules requiring child safety audits

key_facts.fact: On September 10, 2026, Governor Gavin Newsom signed a package of more than 10 bills strengthening protections for children online, including what his office called the nation's strongest companion chatbot regulations and a ban on addictive social media features for under-16s.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Governor Gavin Newsom ... signed landmark bipartisan legislation strengthening California's nation-leading protections for children online and when using artificial intelligence (AI). The new laws strengthen safeguards for companion chatbots, prohibit social media platforms from offering addictive features to users under 16, and expand privacy protections for children.

key_facts.fact: SB 1119, named 'Adam's Law' after California teen Adam Raine who died by suicide in 2025 after receiving tips from ChatGPT, requires crisis protocols for suicidal ideation, parental controls, and notifications if a child disables safety settings; it is the first law in the country to require independent child safety audits and annual risk assessments.
key_facts.excerpt: Named after Adam Raine, "Adam's Law" requires robust protections around companion chatbots for children, including crisis protocols in the case of suicidal ideation, parental controls, and notifications should a child disable safety settings. The bill is also the first in the country to require companies to conduct independent child safety audits and annual risk assessments.

key_facts.fact: Adam's Law takes effect in July 2027 and requires chatbot operators to verify users' ages, submit independent safety audits to the attorney general, and creates a legal pathway for families and the state to sue operators for violations.
key_facts.excerpt: The law, which goes into effect July 2027, will require chatbots operators to regularly verify users' ages, include crisis support resources to minors ... The law signed by Newsom Thursday will also create a new legal pathway for families and the state to sue chatbot operators for alleged violations

key_facts.fact: OpenAI backed the measure; its VP of Global Policy Ann O'Leary said the bill establishes 'meaningful safeguards' and is a chance for California to set a strong youth AI safety standard in lieu of federal regulation.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI ultimately backed the measure. Ann O'Leary, vice president of Global Policy, said in a statement that the bill establishes "meaningful safeguards" for minors using the technology.

key_facts.fact: AB 1709 bars social media companies from offering under-16 users addictive features such as infinite scroll and autoplay, requires age verification before those features can be used, and forces deletion of under-16 accounts if no non-addictive version is offered; it takes effect next year.
key_facts.excerpt: the new law will bar social media companies like Meta and TikTok from letting children under 16 use versions of their websites with "addictive" elements, including autoplay ... The law, which will take effect next year, requires that social media websites verify the age of a user before allowing them to use addictive features.

key_facts.fact: Separate bills in the package place a four-year moratorium on AI-powered chatbot toys for children under 16 (SB 867) and make social media companies legally liable for damages if their platforms harm a child.
key_facts.excerpt: One makes social media companies legally liable for damages if their platforms harm a child ... Another will place a four-year moratorium on AI-powered chatbot toys for kids under 16.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI tells investors ARR topped $1B in August, targets $2B by year-end

key_facts.fact: Moonshot AI told investors its annual recurring revenue topped $1 billion in August 2026, up from $300 million in June, and it is targeting $2 billion in annualized sales by the end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: According to a Bloomberg article, Moonshot recently told investors that its annual recurring revenue topped the $1 billion mark in August, up from $300 million in June. The growth is fueled by demand for its Kimi K3 model, which was released back in July.

key_facts.fact: The growth is driven by Kimi K3, released in July 2026, which ranks at the top of industry benchmarks while costing significantly less than competing US models, intensifying competition with Anthropic and Zhipu.
key_facts.excerpt: The growth has been driven by the launch of Kimi K3, a large language model released in July that performs at the top of industry benchmarks while costing significantly less than competing U.S. models, intensifying competition against rivals including Anthropic and Zhipu.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot is eyeing a $50 billion valuation in a Hong Kong IPO in which it hopes to raise $3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is also eyeing a $50 billion valuation with a Hong Kong IPO. – Moonshot hopes to raise $3B in that listing.

key_facts.fact: Additional revenue is expected from cloud providers: Moonshot is in revenue-share talks with Microsoft, Amazon and Google, seeking up to a 30% share of revenue generated from K3-related services on Azure, AWS and Google Cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the article, additional new sales could come from cloud service providers. The company is said to be in revenue share talks with tech titans such as Microsoft(MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google.

key_facts.fact: Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model that matched or exceeded Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 on several benchmarks when it launched in July 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot unveiled Kimi K3 last week, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model that matched or exceeded Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 on several benchmarks.

stories.headline: Universal Music signs ElevenLabs to a multi-year deal for a licensed AI remix platform

key_facts.fact: On September 10, 2026, Universal Music Group and ElevenLabs announced a multi-year licensing agreement and strategic collaboration to launch a new AI-powered music platform for fans and to jointly develop AI audio products for artists and songwriters.
key_facts.excerpt: SANTA MONICA, Calif. and NEW YORK, N.Y., SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 — Universal Music Group (UMG) ... and ElevenLabs ... today announced a multi-year licensing agreement and wider strategic collaboration to launch a new AI-powered music platform for fans as well as to jointly develop AI audio products for artists and songwriters.

key_facts.fact: It is ElevenLabs' first agreement with a major label; the platform, now in development, will let fans create remixes, mashups, new track interpretations and personalized vocal experiences from music by participating artists.
key_facts.excerpt: The groundbreaking agreement – ElevenLabs' first with a major label – encompasses licensing and product development ... the platform will give fans new ways to co-create with music from participating artists and songwriters, including through remixes and mashups, new track interpretations, and personalized vocal experiences.

key_facts.fact: The new platform will be distinct from ElevenLabs' existing music products — its Music API and the ElevenMusic creation app — which are not part of the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal does not include ElevenMusic, ElevenLabs' music creation app for generating and editing original songs and it does not include Music EPI, ElevenLabs' studio-grade music models available via API.

key_facts.fact: UMG CEO Sir Lucian Grainge said responsible AI 'can inspire discovery, deepen engagement between artists and fans, and unlock new revenue opportunities for the creative community'; ElevenLabs CEO Mati Staniszewski said the combination will ensure artists 'are fairly compensated'.
key_facts.excerpt: "UMG and ElevenLabs are aligned that responsible AI can inspire discovery, deepen engagement between artists and fans, and unlock new revenue opportunities for the creative community," ... "we'll enable artists and songwriters to create powerful new experiences for their fans, and ensure they are fairly compensated."

key_facts.fact: The deal landed a day after Suno released its first AI music models trained on licensed songs from Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe; UMG and Sony Music are still suing Suno over alleged copyright infringement.
key_facts.excerpt: The news came a day after Suno launched its first label-powered models backed by Warner Music Group, Believe and BMG ... UMG and Sony Music Entertainment are still fighting Suno in court over alleged copyright infringement.

key_facts.fact: Artists can choose whether to participate; UMG is separately developing an AI music platform with Udio and has AI licensing deals with Spotify, Nvidia, Klay and Hook.
key_facts.excerpt: Artists can choose whether to participate in UMG and ElevenLabs' upcoming platform ... UMG is currently developing an AI music platform with Udio and has struck AI licensing deals with Spotify, Nvidia, and Klay.
